tips.comment:
Handicapper has given him a chance here. Dropping him 3lbs for his last run. Which in truth wasn't a bad effort. 
He ran a decent enough race lto. Bumping into the Irish challenger Impero. Beaten 10L by the winner admittedly. He did pull 11L clear of the 3rd horse however. 
He boasts a win and 2 places from 5 runs at this track. With the win coming off a 2lbs lower mark than this. He's got a little bit of work to do to reverse form with Just Dottie based on his penultimate run. Having finished 5L behind that horse. He's 5lbs better off with that horse this time. 
The yard are in fine fettle at the moment. The ground is in his favour. He should go well on these terms.

The step up in trip should do the trick for Western Clouds, who comes here with a great chance under top jockey Bowen for a trainer he works very well with. Western Clouds has finished 4th on the last couple of starts but had promised more.

The model I run suggests Power of Words can win this one. Power of Words lines up here with the highest RPR of the limited experience 9 runner field. It does not look overly penalized for it in the weights, and the early market looks open too. Power of Words was 5th last time out 27 days ago but has shown some consistency in the form figures compared to the other runners. The model has issued a 'moderate' stake indicator, which translates to a 1pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This has been driven by a mix of a small gap back to second but good value on offer at 6.5s.

The model I run suggests Nathan Wells can cause an upset in this one. This result has been driven by Nathan Wells having a comparably high RPR to the other 7 runners but has an official ranking that is the lowest. This subsequently means Nathan Wells goes out carrying the lowest amount of weight around this 2m 4f round trip. Last out 19 days ago, so race fitness shouldn't be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

I'm not sure we will see a much better switcher of yards, with the previous trainer not having a winner for 408 days. We saw the eight-year-old finish third over C&D in last year's edition of this race off a 13lb higher mark and I will be staggered if Pauling can't improve him. They can't be travelling all this way for nothing and I'm expecting it to go off favourite.

The model I run suggests Malangen can win this one and cause an upset. This result has been driven by Malangen having the second highest RPR of the 12-horse race but has an official ranking that leaves him looking well treated off this mark. Has shown glimpses of coming back into form with figures of 60-543 and getting closer to getting over the line first. Last out 11 days ago, so race fitness shouldn't be a concern. Needs to find a bit more. Jockey relieves 3 lbs, which helps around this 2m 4f trip and is a prior course and distance winner, so knows how to get it done around this track. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Shantou Lucky won comfortably over course and distance last September by ten lengths. He has been out of form since, including last time after wind surgery, but he has now been dropped two pounds below his winning mark last September and should be capable of being competitive.

The model I run suggests Ballydangan can win this one. This result has been driven by Ballydangan having a comparably high RPR to the other runners in this 12-horse race, but an official ranking that leaves him looking fairly well treated off this mark. Goes out carrying over a stone less than current market favorite Bumpy Evans and even more weight lighter than the top weight. Has shown signs of form when coming first 19 days ago and looks to get over the line first again here. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Burgundy Man can win this one. This result has been driven by Burgundy Man having a comparably high RPR to the other runners in this 10-horse field but an official ranking that leaves him looking relatively well treated off. Goes out carrying just shy of 1 stone less than the current market favorite and top weight over this 2m 7f trip. Form looks to be improving with a good second when last time out 24 days ago and looks to go one better here. Model has issued a 'very low' stakes indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Won a Ripon novice well latest. Moves into a nursery today but can win again. My NB selection here today.

Exceptionally well-drawn in 6 with a prominent running style. With several other front-runners in the field, a strong early pace is expected, but his excellent gate speed should allow him to get into a good rhythm without being burnt up. Rated 72, he looks well handicapped for a horse that has shown good early dash and has plenty of scope for improvement in first handicap.

Just five career runs for the 4yo filly and still unexposed. Two runs this year, both in handicap company, and she hasn’t been beaten far in both races. Plenty of winners have come out of those two races, she runs off the same mark again and William Buick taking over in the saddle is a big positive.

Three runs this year for the 3yo, getting his act together two weeks ago over this 7f trip. Smoothly hitting the front a furlong out and was an easy 2L winner in the end. He can take another step forward and a 4lb higher mark might not stop him from following up.

Really unlucky LTO after bumping into some traffic when travelling very well into the race. Trainer is in form at the moment and I think 6/1 are good odds considering they've only left a 9-day gap between runs. Playing EW.

The 5yo mare has good career stats over this 5f C/D. Back from a 4-month break two weeks ago, maybe going a little too quick when making the running and outpaced late on, but she saw the race out. She faced rivals rated 79-85 that day, now up against 57-75 rated runners. With the jockey’s claim in this apprentice riders’ handicap, she’s effectively 7lb better off now.
Glory Fighter is very versatile as far as trip and ground go. So the quicker going here won't hinder chances of making it 2 wins in 3 runs after a win at Nottingham and a third at Catterick.

Arrives in hot form looking for a third win in 5 starts. Proven C&D winner at Haydock, possessing a crucial prominent running style that often excels over this stiff 5f on good ground. While drawn slightly lower, his early speed and consistency should allow apprentice Farmer to quickly get him into a good stalking position on the stands' side rail. Remains well treated on his recent efforts and should be right in the mix.

Makes a highly intriguing debut for trainer Kevin Ryan, who boasts a strike rate of 67% in this exact 6f fillies' maiden at Haydock over the last 5 years. By the top-class Lope De Vega and out of a mare who won at 2yo, she has the pedigree to be an early, smart type. Stall 7 is also an asset on this straight course on good ground.

Just five career runs for the 3yo and room for improvement. He was a decent 3rd on his handicap debut during May. Only 6th of 12 last time out over 12f, but he still held every chance a furlong out despite being keen in the race. The winner that day is now rated 86 and he shouldn’t fear these 62-68 rated runners over this shorter trip.

At 6 years old she is the oldest horse in the race against the rest of the field who are all 3 year olds. She is 4 times a winner at this track, three times over course and distance and that winning experience could stand her in good stead here.

Backing Saliko, the lightly raced 3-year-old bay filly by Kameko, now trained by Jack Jones, in tomorrow’s Mark Sumner Handicap over 1m 2f 23y at Yarmouth. She arrives in good form after consistent maidens??'finishing third at Beverley (28 May) and second at Brighton (8 May)??'both over around 7 furlongs on good ground, showing she's sharp and has potential to step up successfully in trip .
This rise to middle distances suits her pedigree and recent stamina signs, and though stepping into handicap company, her current mark of 68 looks fair given her promise.
Roman Emperor got back to winning ways at this course last week and could be worth sticking with, going up a furlong in trip.

The trainer places her horses selectively, and her last runner was a winner. She is using a promising 5lb claiming apprentice here who has been picking up rides for the Gosden stable, and he looks good value for his claim. The first-time cheekpieces could be the key here, which are added to the tongue tie. The first time the tongue tie was used resulted in the horse's best run when 3rd of 9 under a very similar trip and ground as she gets here. Crucially, the horses around her that day would suggest she could have plenty in hand off this mark of 54 (she could be a high 60s horse on that evidence).

A former course and distance winner who led for a long way over a mile under today's jockey in an apprentice race last time out. The drop in trip will suit and races off a pound lower mark. Laura Coughlan can claim her 3-pound allowance today, which puts Spanish Mane on an attractive mark.

Came up against a good one when runner-up on racecourse debut behind the odds-on favourite Hope Queen at Beverley 9 days ago. She was slow away that day but ran on well when she got the swing of things and looks the one to beat here.
The drop back to 5f will suit speester Museum Piece who has the best single piece of form when winning on penuultimate start. The 6f trip was not ideal last time.

Kodi Island could be the answer in a tricky race with not much to go on. It must have had a good breeze up, shooting up in price to half a million, and joins a powerful stable related to some decent sorts. It should make a mark.

Backing Reception, the 2-year-old bay colt by Kodi Bear trained by Charlie Fellowes, in tomorrow’s Weatherbys EBF Maiden Stakes (6f). He showed promise on debut at Windsor on June 2, finishing 5th of 13 after being well-backed at 12/1, then stepped up to 4th of 13 at Chester on June 13, beaten just 2¼ lengths . Despite being green early, he improved as the race progressed, suggesting there’s plenty of untapped ability to come ??' and both performances were in solid Class 4 maiden company.
Reception looks to have taken each outing in his stride, and a smooth ride tomorrow should see him break sharper and settle midfield before building his run late on Yarmouth’s straight 6f track.

Thrice raced daughter of Kodiac & Woodland Maiden ( Dam's sire Mastercraftsman ) who was last seen at Bath 19 days ago where finishing a respectable 3rd/10 makes her handicap debut here off a very attractive mark of 70 and she can progress very well now heading down the handicap route and this class 5 nursery handicap is the perfect starting point for this individual steps up in trip here racing at the 7 furlong trip for the first time that most certainly being a good move by her connections as this new trip can bring out further improvement and she is open to plenty of progress and has shaped with promise that this trip will be spot on ideal jockey Hector Crouch takes the ride on Ollie Sangster's inmate and can give Whisperwood a promising ride here at Kempton and jockey Hector Crouch is worth following at this meeting here tonight with a couple of promising rides at disposal that I have found of great interest and will be available on my selections list best of luck to all following and good day to all

Gelded son of Invincible Army & Roger Sez ( Dam's sire Red Clubs ) who was last seen at this venue 79 days ago racing at the 7 furlong trip where finishing 5th/10 arrives here in top nick and in very good heart now dropping back down in trip to the 6 furlong trip here at Kempton that being a good move by his connections as a race of this nature here at the polytrack of Kempton can really suit R M Beckett's inmate well now returned to a sprinting distance currently operating on a mark of 68 this individual should have a much bigger performance in the locker just waiting to unleashed and he should be capable of much better than a mark of 68 so from this point on in my point of view he should leave this mark well behind jockey Hector Crouch takes the ride and can give Invincible Melody the perfect ride here at Kempton merits serious consideration here

The 7yo is capable on his day, 1st or 2nd in 14 races and is a previous C/D winner. Excuses last time out but ran a decent race at this track two starts back. He has a good low draw and he was rated 9lb higher this time last year - now has added help with a good apprentice taking off a handy 7lb.

Runner-up over half a furlong further at Chester at the end of May when last seen, but won over course and distance in the race subsequent to that. Just 4 pounds higher than that course and distance win, and the runner-up has won since too, to boost the form.

Backing Incensed, the 4-year-old Ulysses filly now trained by Amanda Perrett, in tomorrow’s 12f Class 3 Kempton Handicap (6:58 GMT). She returns off a solid reappearance outing at Sandown on June 13, where she finished 5th of 8 over 1m 1f??'the first run since her transfer from Andrew Balding and a near 9-month break, marking her as race-sharp and building .
Her profile shines more brightly in the all-weather sphere: she’s already notched an AW win in September 2024 at Kempton over this same 1m 3f 219y trip, scoring by an impressive 4 lengths . That effort showcases her ability to handle the Kempton surface and suggests she’s well-suited returning to this course and trip.
Stepping back into Class 3 company, she looks well-treated on a mark of 83, especially now on her favoured AW surface, with fitness and confidence under the belt. Expect her to settle in midfield before delivering a telling move in the final furlong. With trainer Amanda Perrett finding form and the race shaping up to suit a proven AW performer, she offers solid each-way value in a competitive field.

Three places and a win in the last five runs since changing yard back in February. The win back in May came here in a field of eleven before a decent 3rd last time out at Lingfield. Has another decent draw here to boost things further.
Has won three of her last seven races, and the 2 lbs increase for her latest win at Chepstow might not be enough to stop her following up here.

One win and two places in three attempts over course and distance bodes well. Drops in trip after racing over the extended seven furlongs at Chester last time out and Elizabeth Gale in the saddle claims a valuable 7 pound allowance for this top weight.

Highly promising gelded son of Havana Gold & Midnight Sky ( Dam's sire Desert Prince ) who very impressively completed a 5 timer of back to back wins towards the end of 2024 was last seen at Yarmouth 35 days ago where finishing 6th/7 however that was his seasonal reappearance run after a 124 day break and he is most certainly entitled to strip fitter and be a lot sharper at the finish this time out with that run under his belt and Havana Sky will highly appreciate this switch to a polytrack surface as he is a much better performer on the polytrack surface rather than the turf currently operating on a mark of 67 E A L Dunlop's inmate looks poised to bounce back here and he is only operating 1lb above his last winning mark here however the last time he won he was a 3yo now as a 4yo this individual should have plenty more performances in the locker just waiting to be unleashed and he can be much better than a mark 67 now as a 4yo jockey Hector Crouch takes the ride and can give this a good shot must be considered

The Tony Carroll 8yo is in fine fettle winning 3 times in the last fortnight and comes here to make it 4. Plenty of weight to carry but Matthew Slater rides again as he has the last 3 times, takes off an important 5lb, and there is no reason to suggest his winning will stop here.
The 4yo is on top of his game, going close in his last three races, the winner from each of those races having won again since. Weighted to run a big race and worth another chance.
Having previously won off much higher marks, Faustus is worth an each-way punt to return to form. If that is the case, the nap can push the hot favorite all the way.

Vocal Legend caught the eye on the latest start when upped in trip to 7f, going down by 1 length at Doncaster. Up 1lb for that run, and can build on that run here to land the first turf success in four starts for trainer Charles Hills.
A beaten favourite over a mile at Kempton last time out and of interest dropping in trip and trying 7 furlongs for the first time.

An open-looking handicap where Imperial Trooper makes some appeal at a big-looking 16/1. He has dropped to a good mark and could get his own way out in front. The drop back in trip looks a good move and wasn't beaten far on his last outing at Sandown in a similar race.

Two turf runs for the 4yo this year. Something amiss last time out. He was a good 3rd of 12 during May after coming off a 4 month break and that form looks decent. A 2lb lower mark now, good jockey booking, every chance in this company and too early to write off.

Lightly raced 4yo. He’s not done a lot wrong in his last two starts, no clear passage two runs back and was too far back for a serious challenge last time out. He is down to a handy looking mark now. Just one previous run on quick ground, on his debut last Aug, when going close and posting a high RPR rating.

This horse got within a length of a couple of 82-rated horses in his first two runs. This well-bred gelding could be seriously well in here on debut for a stable that is flying with their small stable at the moment. The horse races off just 64 now, and the trainer has given the horse a 3-month break before racing the horse. The booking of Fallon suggests he means business. Looks way overpriced to me at 18/1 (and currently friendless in the early market).

Siouxfonic is a 4-year-old son of Sioux Nation ex Velvet Ribbon. He makes his racecourse debut in this 4-year-olds only bumper as a colt. He'll be ridden by Mr. P.W. Mullins for T. Cooper. He wears a tongue tie on this, his debut outing. He may be one for your horse tracker. I make him my Nap of the day.

This J P O'Brien trained 5-y-o gelding won over one mile on soft ground at Listowel back in 2022 and has been mostly running over hurdles since. The latest was 32 days ago over one mile five furlongs on good ground on the flat when only beaten 3/4 length in third of the nine runners behind the H De Bromhead trained Gentleman Joe. So, down in trip and with Mr J L Gleeson onboard, he should prove hard to beat.

The jockey booked on this one has won 3 of his last 12 rides for the stable, and the horse has slipped to his lowest mark since finishing 3rd of 19 at Punchestown last year. Straight after that, he was sent off as short as 7/2 for this jockey when unseating him early. That was off 105, so he's 2lb lower now, and rather than getting 7/2, we are getting 40/1. So, I think it's fairly easy to make a case for the horse being the value here.

Can't get much lower in the weights, this one, and has some fine form at Bellewstown. Gets in here receiving substantial weight from most of the opposition and has a couple of good recent efforts accompanied by today's jockey. Has beaten 3-year-old horse in Hangars, so this 4-year-old plus only race looks a good place at least opportunity given this horse's aforementioned credentials.
Only Spoofing still has ability, having already won this year and has won before off much higher ratings. Worth chancing each way in case a return to form is imminent.
